subject: physics

items.q: In simple harmonic motion, where is acceleration greatest?
items.correct: At maximum displacement; it is zero at the equilibrium position.
items.misconception: It stays constant throughout the motion.
items.random_wrong: It is greatest at the centre of the motion.
items.why: In SHM a = −ω²x: acceleration is proportional to displacement, so it peaks at the extremes.

items.q: Does a simple pendulum's period depend on the mass of the bob?
items.correct: No — for small swings it depends on length and g, not mass.
items.misconception: Yes, a heavier bob gives a longer period.
items.random_wrong: It depends only on how hard you push it.
items.why: T = 2π√(L/g); mass and (small) amplitude don't affect the period.

items.q: Where is the restoring force largest in SHM?
items.correct: At maximum displacement; it is zero at equilibrium.
items.misconception: At the centre of the motion.
items.random_wrong: There is no restoring force in SHM.
items.why: The restoring force is proportional to displacement, so it's zero in the middle and maximal at the ends.
